complexity_ledger.justification: No representation added and none needed. MF-029 is deliberately a GENERATOR change, not a model change: parameters are recovered from each case's own before/after state pair, which the generator already held. TLC re-measured at 231,621 distinct / depth 25 / bound 699,840 (70.0%), identical to the MF-028 baseline, and `git diff origin/epic/modular-fuzzing -- '*.tla' '*.cfg'` is empty. Zero delta is the required outcome here, not merely an acceptable one: the owner rejected a lastInternalAction marker precisely because max_state_space_bound is at 70% and MF-019 proved a single boolean variable breaches it.

refinement.detail: Searched, and found none this ticket should apply. The analyzer's standing recommendation remains to project [lastCommand, result], which no configured invariant reads. MF-028 recorded a strong second argument for it and still declined; that reasoning is unchanged and MF-029 adds no new evidence for or against it. MF-029 adds one argument AGAINST applying it now: this ticket makes action arguments available to adapters for the first time, so the next tickets will be extending what a case genuinely checks. Shrinking the checked surface in the same window as widening it would confound the two effects and make the resulting kill-rate movement uninterpretable. Deferred to MF-023, where decomposition revisits the projection with per-component state spaces. Doctrine also bars it independently: a DECREASE requires all three retention members retained, and all three are non-passing above.

effect_conformance.evidence: CARRIED FORWARD from MF-028. Adapters drive the CLI via subprocess.run; the sandbox observes only the in-process CPython runtime, so the target is structurally invisible. MF-027's refusal stands. MF-029 changes generated case PARAMETERS only and no adapter consumes them yet, so the observability barrier is untouched.

summary: MF-029: recover action parameters from each case's before/after state pair, generator-side. Zero TLA+ model delta. Audited all 14 action labels plus Stutter: 9 guard-pinned, 5 except-index, 1 written-through (ScaffoldProject, the only action that sacrifices an after-state check), 1 UNRECOVERABLE (RunSpecUnitTests override) marked UNCHECKED and never fabricated. 14/14 negative controls verified to fail; 6/6 implementation mutations caught after closing an initially-surviving before-vs-after mutation. No case dropped: 798,411 TLC transitions in, 798,411 cases out.

assertions: generated cases carry real params for every action where recovery is possible, derived from the state pair.
a per-action recoverability audit covers ALL THIRTEEN labels, naming the mechanism used (guard-pinned / except-index / written-through) or the reason recovery is impossible.
parameters that cannot be recovered are marked UNCHECKED, never fabricated; an action whose parameters are entirely unrecoverable is reported as a finding.
a negative-control test per action proves the parameter check can actually fail -- the regression guard against the tautology MF-028 caught in itself.
ZERO TLA+ model delta; if the model appears to need changing, the ticket STOPS and reports rather than reopening a decision the owner already made.
no case is dropped, filtered or skipped because its parameters could not be recovered -- mark and keep.

ticket.objective: All 57,617 generated cases carry params={} -- the generator records THAT an action fired, not WITH WHAT. Until fixed, every downstream adapter fix buys reachability testing rather than argument testing, which for a CLI is most of the point. THIS IS A GENERATOR CHANGE, NOT A MODEL CHANGE. Adding a lastInternalAction marker was considered and REJECTED by the owner: unnecessary, because parameters are recoverable from the case own before/after state pair which the generator already has; and unaffordable, because max_state_space_bound is at 70% and MF-019 proved a boolean variable breaches it, so a marker carrying action names plus argument bindings would force decomposition before it could land. Being generator-side is also what makes this experimental and cheaply revertible, an explicit condition of approval -- nothing in the spec changes and reverting is deleting a function. Recovery verified across three mechanisms: GUARD-PINNED (OpenTicket root, via the guard root = spec_root), EXCEPT-INDEX (ticket, via ticket_state EXCEPT ![ticket]), and WRITTEN-THROUGH (ScaffoldProject root, via spec_root in the after-state). THE TRAP: MF-028 wrote a tautology into its own work, defaulting spec_root from case.after then checking against case.after, which passed vacuously and was caught only because a negative control that should have failed passed. Derive from the BEFORE-state and the transition, never from the field being checked; mark unrecoverable parameters UNCHECKED rather than fabricating a value; and require a negative control per action, because a check that cannot fail is not a check. See tickets/029-infer-action-parameters.md.
